status: Throwaway feasibility experiment, not integrated or deployed. Earlier local implementation remains unchanged.
question: Does a real first-success race of authenticated CDN-to-Telegram delivery and current acquisition/upload reduce completion latency while stopping losers?

method.selection: Fixed before running: previous sample IDs 1,2,4,7,8,10,11,12. Four reels (including 75s and 90s), one single photo, two-photo album, twelve-photo album, eleven-item mixed album. Includes previous failure cases.

modes.race: Direct authenticated metadata/CDN URL worker and current worker start together.
modes.hedged: Direct starts immediately; current starts after 8 seconds, or immediately if direct fails sooner.

method.order: Rotate current/race/hedged order per sample. Three seconds between cases. One measured trial per URL/mode.
method.accounts: 16 distinct initially eligible saved-session accounts, separate pinned direct/current account per URL. Same per-branch account across modes, private state per branch, copied sessions; production state not changed.
method.isolation: Single benchmark container, 2 CPUs, 1 GB RAM, instagrapi3.0.16 and current local source snapshot, production network namespace, configured storage chat only.
method.winner_contract: All media must be staged with Telegram file IDs before a branch is ready. A failed branch never wins. Coordinator selects one ready result, stops/reaps running losers, then invokes the existing final sender once. It never switches winner after a final-send failure.
method.cancellation: SIGTERM asks child coroutine to cancel and run existing subprocess cleanup; after 3 seconds hard-kill remaining tracked descendants, including workers in separate sessions. Record cleanup latency and remaining live processes.
method.timing: Parent trial start through acknowledgement of all final sends, including worker startup/imports, bot setup, provider work, storage staging, loser cleanup and final sender. Excludes incoming Telegram update queue/intake.
method.validation_tests: Eight controlled tests passed: first-success selection, failed branch, delayed backup, avoided backup, ties, all failures, deadlines, external cancellation/nested process cleanup, plus photo/video staging dispatch (some cases combined).

excluded_pilot.reason: Photo/video dispatch indentation error in throwaway harness. Stopped, fixed and regression-tested before complete restart. Pilot results are not included in summaries.

limitations: Historical prototype only: later review found readiness published after teardown, incomplete cleanup of late-spawned descendants, and eligibility/state confounds. Its measurements and test counts are preserved as observations, not validation of the integrated coordinator. Prototype sources are archived in git commit 9996a40 and removed from the active tree.
One small, deliberately mixed convenience sample; no confidence interval, production percentile guarantee or sustained multi-user load validation.
Current branch uses a different account from direct for concurrency safety. Account/proxy differences may affect relative performance; same branch account reused across modes.
Direct bypasses full decode/remux. Readiness confirms Telegram staging plus metadata compatibility, not physical-device playback or full source integrity.
Direct photos choose largest candidate; current photo dimensions were not measured. Photo quality is not identical across paths.
Repeated historical URLs may be warm in Telegram/CDN caches. Order rotates, but network/cache variance remains.
Cancellation proves local workers stopped. It cannot revoke a request already accepted by Telegram or Instagram; redundant storage-chat staging can remain.
One coordinator final-send invocation prevents competing branches from sending. It does not establish distributed exactly-once delivery after network timeouts or process crashes.
Benchmark private per-process account/concurrency state is not a production-wide governor. Integration needs shared account leases, provider/upload limits and a cap on speculative jobs.
Successful-only latency summaries exclude failures; all trial failures remain in results.
Outer process startup is included here, unlike the preceding 12-link benchmark. Compare modes within this experiment.

official_constraints.fact: Telegram documents HTTP URL sending limits of 5 MB for photos and 20 MB for other content, correct MIME type, and no changing media type when resending file IDs. Exact applicability/error cause in local Bot API must be verified from returned errors.

targeted_three_way_follow_up.method: After the 24-trial comparison, add a third immediately-started public-only yt-dlp download/normalize/upload worker on four selected URLs. Uses same eight-sample account assignment, copied fresh state, same two-CPU container budget. Public worker never acquires/logs into an account. Current branch still has its own sequential public fallback, so duplicate public work is possible.

targeted_three_way_follow_up.limitations: Targeted follow-up, not a complete eight-link comparison or a repeated randomized trial. Increased concurrent normalization can compete for two allocated CPUs.

overlapping_delivery_and_cleanup_follow_.method: Repeat the two video cases with the same three branches. Start loser shutdown tasks together and let the single final-send callback run concurrently; retain all worker ownership and wait for cleanup before returning from the coordinator. Only cleanup/delivery scheduling changed.
overlapping_delivery_and_cleanup_follow_.tests: All eight original coordinator/staging tests plus two overlap tests passed: ten tests. A controlled worker ignoring SIGTERM proves final sending starts while cleanup waits, and all-failed candidates never invoke final delivery.

overlapping_delivery_and_cleanup_follow_.interpretation: In the 90-second reel trial final Telegram acknowledgement occurred at35.092s, while coordinator cleanup finished at37.751s; this directly demonstrates 2.659s of cleanup kept out of recipient latency. Total differences against earlier trials also include network/provider variability and must not be attributed solely to scheduling.

findings: Two-way immediate race delivered8/8 versus current8/8. Successful medians9.692s versus21.577s; median paired percentage reduction30.59%. Worst case increased52.333s versus47.706s. These statistics describe this sample only.

Eight-second hedge launched13 candidate jobs versus16 for immediate racing (18.75% fewer), delivered7/8, and had58.205s worst successful delivery. One failed mixed-album trial does not establish a failure-rate estimate or prove delay caused failure.

Two-way winners: direct5, current3. Five losing current workers stopped in0.1876–0.2494s, with zero remaining live tracked processes. One coordinator final-send invocation per successful trial; no competing branch final sends.

Three-way race improved the12-photo album from45.2s (two-way) to31.021s (public won), but worsened the90-second reel from21.141s to39.217s. Current-path normalization increased from6.227s to17.467s under the extra branch; consistent with CPU contention, not a controlled causal isolation.

Silent MP4s in the mixed album produced Telegram animation/document fields and no video field via URL. They were rejected as unusable video candidates before final delivery. Current local upload delivered the complete album in some trials. Racing cannot treat every successful Telegram response as the required media type.

The90-second reel repeatedly received Telegram Failed to get http url content for URL fetch. Its local normalized payload was24,190,666bytes, above the documented20MB URL limit; size is a plausible explanation, not independently proven by the generic error.

Delivery can overlap losing-worker cleanup safely within the prototype single-committer contract. Resource slots/leases must remain owned until workers actually stop. This removes cleanup from recipient latency without promising remote cancellation or distributed exactly-once delivery.

recommendation.approach: Proceed toward a bounded, media-aware first-success race; do not unconditionally launch three full pipelines or adopt an untested universal eight-second hedge.
requirements: Only one coordinator can invoke final delivery; select complete staged media, ignore branch failures, and do not switch after ambiguous/partial final sends.
Start loser cancellation and final delivery concurrently, but release worker capacity/account leases only after shutdown completes.
Check URL-fetch size, media type and compatibility before any album staging; route silent-video/oversized cases to local upload.
Use independent public extraction selectively to avoid waiting through a failing authenticated chain; share extraction results so branches cannot repeat the same public work.
Share account leases, Telegram flood/backoff limits and provider capacity across branches; cap expensive normalization, and reuse already staged matching items rather than uploading them again.
Validate sustained multi-user load, account health and device playback before deployment.
recommendation.status: Recommendation and throwaway experiments only; no production integration or deployment in this turn.
